summary: The Main Street Depositor Protection Act amends the Federal Deposit Insurance Act and the Federal Credit Union Act to provide federal deposit insurance for certain noninterest-bearing transaction accounts. It directs the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) to issue a rule establishing a maximum insurance amount between the standard maximum and $5,000,000 for these accounts, with certain exclusions for global systemically important bank holding companies and foreign bank branches. Credit unions are also included under parallel rules. Furthermore, the bill outlines a 10-year transition period for phasing in the calculation of these insured deposits and exempts certain smaller depository institutions from specific special assessments during this transition.

affected_groups.effect: Receive federal deposit insurance coverage for noninterest-bearing transaction accounts up to a new limit established by rule between the standard maximum and $5,000,000.
Are exempt during the transition period from paying certain special assessments or assessment increases related to the extended insurance coverage.
affected_groups.group: Smaller Depository Institutions (assets of $10,000,000,000 or less)

affected_groups.effect: Are explicitly excluded from having their noninterest-bearing transaction accounts covered by the new higher insurance limits.
affected_groups.group: Global Systemically Important BHCs and Foreign Bank Branches

key_provisions: Requires the FDIC to issue a rule establishing extra deposit insurance for noninterest-bearing transaction accounts, capped between the standard deposit insurance amount and $5,000,000.

Excludes insured depository institutions that are subsidiaries of global systemically important bank holding companies or insured branches of foreign banks from receiving this specific extra insurance.
Applies parallel deposit insurance rules to insured credit unions through the National Credit Union Administration Board.

Establishes a 10-year transition period during which the FDIC and the National Credit Union Administration Board must phase in the inclusion of these insured deposits into their respective funding calculations.
Exempts depository institutions with total assets of $10,000,000,000 or less from certain special assessments or assessment increases during the transition period.
missing_information: The exact maximum insurance amount between the standard amount and $5,000,000, as it is left to be determined by an FDIC rule.

It directs the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) to issue a rule establishing a maximum insurance amount between the standard maximum and $5,000,000 for these accounts, with certain exclusions for global systemically important bank holding companies and foreign bank branches. Credit unions are also included under parallel rules. Furthermore, the bill outlines a 10-year transition period for phasing in the calculation of these insured deposits and exempts certain smaller depository institutions from specific special assessments during this transition.
summary_detail.significance: The bill provides a regulatory framework to protect noninterest-bearing transaction accounts above standard insurance limits up to $5,000,000 at eligible institutions, impacting how bank and credit union deposits are insured and assessed over a 10-year transition period.
